def.brief: Amend one test rs-tests wrote, before any build: test_Q_strict_sites_source_state_tests_an_untracked_or_ignored_directory_as_a_directory expects a change inside a git-ignored plain directory (custom-record.json/ under /custom-record.json/ in .gitignore, no .git inside) to stale an eyes answer. source_state hashes git-visible source only; it examines ignored directory entries from git status solely to find nested repositories (a probe on the current tree: an ignored plain directory's change leaves the fingerprint as it was, an ignored nested repository's change moves it). Q-strict-sites 3 says such an entry is 'tested as a directory (with its trailing /), so a file entry never prunes it' — it does not make ignored plain directories source. Make the ignored custom-record.json/ a nested git repository (git init inside it, child.py committed there), so the test decides whether the bare custom-record.json prunes an ignored repository of that name; keep the untracked hunsu.json/ part as it is. The test must still fail on the current tree (python3 test_dwitbuk.py or a focused python3 -c 'import test_dwitbuk as t; t.test_...()'; python3 -m unittest collects nothing here). Change nothing else; change no file but test_dwitbuk.py; do not commit.

I also ran a separate probe, not part of the file, on just the ignored nested-repository case. There too a change to `custom-record.json/child.py` leaves consume at exit 0, so both halves of the test fail now because the feature is missing, not because of a fault in the test. No other file or test was changed, and nothing was committed.

disputed-tests.contract_quote: The diff is composed from the candidate file paths git reports as changed against the same base
disputed-tests.why: The fixture's first review starts at the lock commit, before child.py files existed. late_packet supplies no --since override, so eyes uses that review's since. Git correctly reports both children as new files, but the test requires '-hchild = 1' and '-cchild = 1', which require the later directory commit as base. The fixture should explicitly select dirs_base for those assertions; changing production base selection would exceed this slice.

response.summary:
The builder's dispute was right, and I fixed the test. Only test_Q_strict_sites_eyes_request_diff_holds_children_of_a_replaced_file_on_real_git_output in test_dwitbuk.py changed. Its first eyes request used to be made through late_packet with no base given, so the review's own starting point was used. That point is before the child.py files were committed. The test still required '-hchild = 1' and '-cchild = 1', which only hold when the base is the commit that holds the directories. The fixture now runs `eyes request --out <packet> --since dirs_base --target <project>` and checks the exit is 0. The diff and new_files assertions after it are unchanged, and so is the second request from files_base. Nothing else was changed and nothing was committed.

Results: on the current build the fixed test passes when run alone. In a clean copy of HEAD's code (git archive) with the new test file, it fails with an AssertionError, so the test does decide the feature. The full check, `python3 test_dwitbuk.py`, exits 1 because one test outside this slice fails: test_session_start_hook_says_what_the_placed_reviews_still_need_and_nothing_else, with a JSONDecodeError. It also fails in the clean HEAD copy, so this fix did not cause it.
